utility.notes: SCE's own 'Incorporated Cities and Counties Served by SCE' fact sheet (updated 3/17/2025) explicitly lists 'Temecula' by name among the cities in its service area.

value.name: Southern California Edison (SCE)
value.notes: Temecula was never a Western Community Energy member city (its member cities were Eastvale, Hemet, Jurupa Valley, Norco, Perris, and Wildomar), and WCE itself deregistered with the CPUC and dissolved via Chapter 9 bankruptcy in 2021 — so no CCA currently operates anywhere in Riverside County. SCE is recorded as both the distribution and generation utility.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Southern California Edison (SCE), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by SCE across its entire distribution territory, which includes Temecula/Riverside County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC-administered SGIP program already confirmed for other SCE-territory records this session, reused as a utility-level fact.

value.name: Digital plan submission meeting the City's Digital Submittal Requirements (CD-3)
Plans and calculations, sealed/signed originals, designed under the 2025 California Building, Electrical, and Energy Codes
Detailed plans for the photovoltaic module array
Plot plan showing array location relative to property lines, setbacks, and locations of disconnects, inverters, and existing electrical meter(s)
Site plan showing sleeping-room egress paths, ridge/roof setbacks, and Rapid Shutdown System (RSS) device initiator location
Labels and signage per CEC 690.56, 690.13, and 705.10
Structural engineering calculations showing panel loads imposed on the roof
Specifications for photovoltaic modules, panels, arrays, framing supports, conduit sizing/location, and wire sizes

required_documents.notes: Per the City's own 'CD31 Residential Photovoltaic Requirements' bulletin (revised 02/06/26, current as of this session).
